Still just an intersection. The garbage truck has left, scooters idle at the red, the breakfast place is frying eggs like always, the tile is still missing.

You stand exactly where he stood. Thirty seconds. Nothing happens.

Weeks later someone posts a photo online — flew in from a long way off just to stand there. The replies are full of people saying they're jealous.

You look at the photo. That's the place you walk through every day without once looking up.

Turns out the difference isn't the intersection.

The difference is that someone was willing to stand there for thirty seconds,

and you've been walking through it with your head down.
en.editorNote: For the person who recognized their own corner in a show; also worth rereading on a day when your city feels boring
variations: Extended: there are aftereffects. You start pausing on walks, framing a corner like a shot — imagining the score, the slow motion. You'd never say it out loud, but the walk really does get easier.

Reversal: there's a disappointing version. You look up where a show was filmed, make the trip, and find the shop closed and the wall repainted. You take a picture. It looks nothing like the scene. You keep it anyway and decide that's fine — the shot lives only in the show now, where nobody can change it.

items.sourceNote: 維基百科逃避主義條目關於透過虛構世界短暫離開當下環境的說明，原創改編為盛夏看雪景劇還把冷氣調低的情境

zh-tw.content:
外面三十四度，你在看一部下雪的劇。

角色縮著脖子，呼出來的氣是白的，圍巾繞了三圈。看著看著，你把冷氣調低了兩度。

沒有人要求你這樣做。你只是覺得，這樣比較對。

然後你去拿了一件薄外套，蓋在腿上。

到第四集，你已經在一個三十四度的夜晚，裹著外套、吹著十九度的冷氣，看別人在雪裡走路。

電費是真的，雪不是。

有趣的是反過來也成立。一月的時候你看一部整季都在海邊的劇，看完會想吃冰。外面在下雨，你身上穿兩件，還是點了外送。

追劇大概是最便宜的換季方式。

不用打包、不用請假、不用查天氣，

躺在原地，你就可以短暫地過一種不屬於這個月份的日子。

隔天早上你把冷氣關掉，走到陽台。

三十四度，蟬在叫，跟昨天一模一樣。

但你昨晚確實去過一個會下雪的地方。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個大熱天看雪景劇還把冷氣往下調的人；也適合在懶得出門旅行的那個週末貼給自己
variations: 延伸版：這套機制連吃的都管。看古裝劇會想吃麵，看日劇會想吃便利商店的飯糰，看北歐的劇你會突然覺得家裡應該要有一鍋湯。你的購物車比你誠實。
反轉版：偶爾也會錯亂。你在冷氣房裡看完一部下雪的劇，開門被熱氣糊了一臉，愣了兩秒才想起現在是八月。那兩秒鐘，你是真的以為外面會冷。

en.content:
It's ninety-three degrees outside and you're watching a show set in the snow.

The characters have their shoulders up around their ears, their breath is white, the scarf goes around three times. Somewhere in the second episode you turn the AC down two degrees.

Nobody asked you to do that. It just felt more correct.

Then you get a light jacket and put it over your legs.

By episode four you are, on a ninety-three-degree night, wrapped in a jacket under a sixty-six-degree vent, watching other people walk through snow.

The electric bill is real. The snow is not.

The funny part is that it runs the other way too. In January you watch a series set entirely on a coast and finish it wanting ice cream. It's raining, you're in two layers, and you order it anyway.

Binge-watching might be the cheapest way to change seasons.

No packing, no time off, no checking the forecast.

You stay exactly where you are and briefly live in a month that isn't this one.

In the morning you turn off the AC and step onto the balcony.

Ninety-three degrees. Cicadas. Identical to yesterday.

But last night you really did go somewhere it snows.
en.editorNote: For the person who turns the AC down to get into a snowbound show; also for the weekend you can't be bothered to travel
variations: Extended: it governs food too. Period dramas make you want noodles. A Japanese series makes you want a convenience-store rice ball. Something Nordic and you suddenly feel your kitchen ought to contain a pot of soup. Your shopping cart is more honest than you are.

Reversal: occasionally it misfires. You finish a snowbound episode in the air conditioning, open the door into a wall of heat, and stand there two full seconds before remembering it's August. For those two seconds you genuinely expected it to be cold.

items.sourceNote: 維基百科第二語言習得條目關於情境與情緒影響詞彙記憶的說明，原創改編為追外語劇只學會台詞卻不會點餐的情境

zh-tw.content:
追了六年的外語劇，你自認多少學了一點。

直到真的要用，你才發現你會的詞長這樣：

「證據」——會。
「請問廁所在哪裡」——不會。

「你騙我」——會，而且語氣有三種。
「這個多少錢」——不會。

「我不會放手」——會，閉著眼睛都會。
「一杯紅茶，半糖少冰」——完全不會。

你學到的不是一種語言，是一份情緒清單。

因為那些詞你不是背起來的，是被一場戲砸進腦子裡的。

有人在雨裡喊過那句，有人在病房外用氣音說過那句，有人講完那句之後三集都沒再出現。

所以那些字對你來說不是字，是畫面。

這聽起來沒什麼用，直到有一年你真的去了那個國家。

你點餐點得很糟，問路問到店員笑出來。

但要離開的那天，在機場有個陌生人對你說了一句很短的話，

你完全聽懂了。

那是你在第十七集學會的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個追外語劇追到會背台詞卻不會點餐的人；也適合在被朋友問「你這樣有學到語言嗎」的時候丟出來
variations: 延伸版：這份清單還有另一半是嘆氣和語助詞。你可能不會自我介紹，但你嘆氣的方式已經完全變成劇裡的樣子，連朋友都聽得出來。
反轉版：也有丟臉的時候。你把劇裡學來的那句順口說出去，對方臉色一變。後來才有人告訴你，那句話在現實生活中只有吵架才會用。

en.content:
Six years of watching shows in a language you don't speak, and you figure you've picked up something.

Then you actually try to use it, and here's the inventory:

"Evidence" — yes.
"Where's the bathroom" — no.

"You lied to me" — yes, in three different tones.
"How much is this" — no.

"I'm not letting go" — yes. In your sleep.
"One iced tea, half sugar, light ice" — absolutely not.

What you learned isn't a language. It's an emotional inventory.

Because you didn't memorize those words. A scene drove them into your head.

Someone shouted one of them in the rain. Someone whispered one outside a hospital room. Someone said one and then didn't appear again for three episodes.

So they aren't words to you. They're images.

Which sounds useless, right up until the year you actually go there.

You order badly. You ask for directions so poorly the clerk laughs.

But on the day you leave, at the airport, a stranger says one short thing to you,

and you understand it completely.

You learned it in episode seventeen.
en.editorNote: For the person who can recite dialogue in a language they can't order lunch in; good ammunition when a friend asks whether you're actually learning anything
variations: Extended: the other half of the list is sighs and filler sounds. You may not be able to introduce yourself, but the way you exhale has completely changed, and your friends can hear it.
Reversal: it can embarrass you. You drop a line you picked up from a show and watch someone's face change. Later a native speaker explains that in real life, people only say that during a fight.

items.sourceNote: 天下雜誌關於追劇如何影響大腦與注意力的報導，原創改編為通勤族在到站前九十秒的抉擇情境

zh-tw.content:
還剩九十秒，車子要到站了。

這是追劇的人每天都要做一次的判斷題。

你算過：這集剩九十秒，走到出口三分鐘，過馬路等紅燈再四十秒。

理論上綽綽有餘。

但劇不是這樣運作的。最後九十秒從來不是收尾，是下一集的開頭。

你的歷史紀錄長這樣：

有一次你在月台上站著看完，旁邊來了又走了兩班車。

有一次你邊走邊看，肩膀撞到柱子，手機差點飛出去。

有一次你決定關掉，結果走出站的那整段路，你的腦子完全不在路上。

還有一次——你沒有下車。

門開了又關，你聽見廣播念出下一站的名字，那時候你才抬頭。

你在心裡替自己找了一個很體面的理由：反正回程也會經過。

其實真正的原因很簡單。

一場戲斷在錯的地方，跟沒看是不一樣的。

你可以晚三分鐘進辦公室，但你沒辦法讓那句話停在一半，然後帶著它去開會。

所以下次螢幕上剩九十秒、車子開始減速的時候，不用罵自己。

你只是一個不想把話聽一半的人。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個為了看完結尾寧願站在月台上不出站的通勤族；也適合在被念「你怎麼又晚到」的時候拿來當抗辯狀
variations: 延伸版：這題還有升級版——剩九十秒，而且你知道這集是大結局。這時候什麼馬路、什麼會議都不存在了，你會在原地把它看完，看完再決定今天要不要當一個正常人。
反轉版：也有你賭錯的時候。你判斷那九十秒只是收尾，結果它丟出全劇最大的轉折。你人已經站在手扶梯上，整個僵住，後面的人一個一個繞過你走。

en.content:
Ninety seconds left, and the train is pulling in.

Every commuter who watches shows makes this call once a day.

You've run the math: ninety seconds on the episode, three minutes to the exit, forty more at the crosswalk.

Plenty of room, in theory.

Shows don't work that way. The last ninety seconds are never the ending. They're the beginning of the next one.

Your record so far:

Once you stood on the platform and finished it while two trains came and went.

Once you walked and watched at the same time, clipped your shoulder on a pillar, nearly launched your phone.

Once you shut it off, and then your head wasn't on the sidewalk for the entire walk home.

And once — you didn't get off.

The doors opened and closed. You heard the announcement name the next station, and only then did you look up.

You gave yourself a dignified reason: the return trip goes through here anyway.

The real reason is simpler.

A scene cut off in the wrong place is not the same as a scene you haven't seen.

You can walk in three minutes late. You cannot let a line stop halfway and then carry it into a meeting.

So the next time it says ninety seconds and the train starts slowing down, go easy on yourself.

You're just someone who doesn't like hearing half of something.
en.editorNote: For the commuter who will stand on the platform rather than leave an episode unfinished; also works as a defense the next time someone asks why you're late
variations: Extended: there's a harder version of this problem. Ninety seconds left, and you know this one is the finale. At that point the street and the meeting stop existing. You finish it where you stand, and then decide whether to be a functional person today.

Reversal: sometimes you bet wrong. You read those ninety seconds as a wind-down, and they deliver the biggest turn in the whole show. You're already on the escalator, frozen, while people step around you one by one.

items.sourceNote: 報導者關於台語八點檔生態與年輕觀眾收視習慣轉變的報導，原創改編為「以前有人幫你決定何時停」的世代對照

zh-tw.content:
以前的追劇，是有人幫你決定什麼時候停的。

八點播，一天一集，四十分鐘後跑片尾，畫面跳出「明天同一時間」。

然後你就得去睡了。不是你有自制力，是沒得看了。

那個年代的廣告時間，也不是拿來浪費的。

第一段，你去把陽台的衣服收進來。

第二段，你被叫去洗碗，還一路抗議說快回來了。

第三段，全家人趁那三分鐘吵完一整天份的架，主題曲一響，大家自動安靜。

一部劇播三個月，你的生活也跟著長出一個固定的形狀。

現在不一樣了。

現在你想看幾集就看幾集。沒有人喊停，沒有片尾跟你說明天見，只有一行「三秒後播放下一集」——而那三秒，根本不夠讓你反悔。

你以為你終於自由了。

結果凌晨兩點，你抱著手機，一邊看一邊在心裡罵自己。

那行你當年最討厭的字——「明天同一時間」——

現在想起來，居然有點溫柔。

它不是在限制你。

它是在替你，把今天收起來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個懷念以前一天只能看一集的朋友；也適合在自己又看到天亮、想找個說法解釋的時候貼出來
variations: 延伸版：那個年代還有一種痛，是錯過了就真的錯過了。隔天到學校，全班都在講昨晚那一段，你只能靠別人的轉述拼出一個大概的版本，然後點頭裝作自己也看到了。
反轉版：也有人不肯認輸。家裡那台會錄的機器就是為了這種時候存在的。你設定好時間才出門，回來滿心期待，發現它錄到一半就跳掉，或者完整錄下了另一台的節目。

en.content:
One episode a day. Someone else decided when you stopped.

Eight o'clock, one episode, forty minutes, then credits and a card that said same time tomorrow.

And then you went to bed. Not discipline. There was simply nothing left.

The commercial breaks weren't wasted either.

First break: you pulled the laundry in off the balcony.

Second break: you got sent to do the dishes, protesting the whole way that it was coming back on.

Third break: the whole family compressed a full day of arguing into three minutes, and when the theme music returned everyone went quiet on their own.

A show ran for three months, and your life grew a shape around it.

Not anymore.

Now you watch as many as you want. Nobody calls time. No credits say see you tomorrow. Just a line that reads next episode in three seconds — and three seconds is not enough time to change your mind.

You thought this was freedom.

Then it's two in the morning, you're holding your phone, watching and quietly insulting yourself.

That card you used to hate — same time tomorrow —

seems almost kind now.

It wasn't limiting you.

It was putting your day away for you.
en.editorNote: For the friend who misses the era of one episode a night; also useful when you've watched until sunrise again and need a way to describe it
variations: Extended: back then there was another kind of pain — miss it and you actually missed it. The next day everyone was talking about last night's scene, and you built a rough version out of secondhand accounts and nodded like you'd seen it.

Reversal: some people refused to lose. The machine that recorded things existed for exactly this. You set the timer before leaving, came home hopeful, and found it cut out halfway through, or captured a different channel in perfect quality.

items.sourceNote: Trip.com 台灣站的節日約會與餐廳攻略，原創改編為情侶放棄外出訂位、留在家一起追劇的情境；內容不寫死節日名稱與日期

zh-tw.content:
那個節日，你們本來也想過要出門。

查了餐廳，看到三個字：已訂滿。

換一家，只剩九點四十五那一輪，而且用餐限時九十分鐘。

再換一家，電話打了三次都在忙線。

你們對看一眼，同時笑出來。

那天晚上，你們哪裡都沒去。

外送點了兩份平常就會點的東西，多加了一份甜的。

冷氣開到有點涼，毯子只有一條，所以要坐得很近。

然後你們打開那部拖了三個禮拜、說好要一起看的劇。

一集看完，中間暫停了四次。

第一次，他去拿水。

第二次，你說「等等，這個人是不是前面出現過」。

第三次，你們為了一個角色的決定吵了五分鐘，誰也沒說服誰。

第四次沒有原因，就只是講到別的事情去了，講了二十分鐘才想起來螢幕還亮著。

那個晚上沒有拍照，沒有打卡，沒有人問你們今天怎麼過的。

但你可能會記得很久。

因為所謂的約會，本來就不是去了哪裡、拍到什麼。

是你們兩個人，願意把一整個晚上，交給同一件事。

而且中間可以隨時暫停。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個決定不跟人擠、留在家裡過節的另一半；也適合在被問「你們節日都不出門喔」的時候直接當回答
variations: 延伸版：這種晚上還有一個好處，是你可以穿家裡最醜的那件衣服。沒有人要拍照，沒有人要看你，你們兩個都放棄形象，然後在沙發上笑得比在任何餐廳都大聲。
反轉版：當然也有翻車的版本。你們挑了一部兩個人都沒看過的劇，結果第一集就很難看。你們互相等對方先開口說「要不要換」，硬撐了三十分鐘，最後同時說出同一句話。

en.content:
Restaurants were the first plan, and the first plan died fast.

You looked one up: fully booked.

The next one had only the nine forty-five seating, with a ninety-minute limit.

The third one, you called three times and got a busy signal.

You looked at each other and laughed at the same moment.

That night you went nowhere.

You ordered the delivery you always order, plus one dessert you don't.

The AC ran a little too cold and there was only one blanket, so you had to sit close.

Then you opened the show you'd been putting off for three weeks, the one you promised to watch together.

One episode. Four pauses.

First pause: he went to get water.

Second: you said wait, have we seen this guy before.

Third: you argued for five minutes about a character's decision and neither of you moved.

Fourth had no reason at all. You drifted onto something else and talked for twenty minutes before remembering the screen was still on.

Nobody took a photo. Nobody posted anything. Nobody asked how your evening went.

You'll probably remember it for a long time anyway.

Because a date was never about where you went or what you photographed.

It's two people willing to hand one whole evening to the same thing.

With the option to pause whenever you want.
en.editorNote: For the partner who decided to skip the crowds and stay in; also a ready answer when someone asks why you two never go out on the day
variations: Extended: an evening like this has one more advantage — you get to wear the ugliest thing you own. Nobody is photographing you, nobody is looking, both of you give up entirely, and you laugh louder on that couch than you would in any restaurant.

Reversal: there is a version where it collapses. You pick something neither of you has seen and the first episode is bad. You each wait for the other to say should we switch, hold out for thirty minutes, and then say the same sentence at the same time.

items.sourceNote: 自由娛樂關於本土八點檔常見劇情套路的專題報導，原創改編為長輩憑多年經驗兩分鐘預測整部劇走向的情境

zh-tw.content:
你媽走進客廳的時候，你已經看到第三集。

她沒有問劇名，沒有問誰是誰，站著看了大概兩分鐘，然後說了三句話：

「這個女的不是他親妹妹。」

「那個穿西裝的活不過一半。」

「他們兩個最後會在一起，但要先分開一次。」

說完她就去洗水果了。

你翻了一個很大的白眼。

第十四集，那個穿西裝的出事了。

第二十三集，身世那條線攤開來，她果然不是。

第三十集，那兩個人分開了。第三十六集，他們回來了。

你坐在沙發上，手裡拿著遙控器，有一種被看穿的感覺——不是被劇看穿，是被你媽看穿。

後來你才想通。

她不是通靈，她只是看過太多了。

那些你嫌老套的東西，她從年輕看到現在，看過幾百次，早就變成一種直覺。

平台有資料庫，她有三十年。

而且她說完就走了，從來不留下來炫耀。

因為她的重點根本不是猜對。

她只是想在你旁邊站兩分鐘，跟你講幾句話。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個被家裡長輩兩分鐘破掉整部劇的人；也適合在長輩又說中一次、你不太想承認的時候拿出來
variations: 延伸版：她的準確度是有範圍的。感情線、家庭線、誰跟誰有關係，幾乎沒失手過。但你放一部推理劇，她會看三分鐘，說一句「這什麼東西」，然後轉身去做別的事。
反轉版：也有換你上場的一天。有天她在看一部新劇，你經過客廳站著看了兩分鐘，脫口說出一個猜測。三集之後你猜中了，她轉頭看你的那個表情，跟你當年一模一樣。

en.content:
Two minutes. That's all your mother needed.

You were already on episode three when she walked into the living room.

She didn't ask what it was called. She didn't ask who anyone was. She stood there for about two minutes and said three things:

"That girl is not actually his sister."

"The one in the suit doesn't make it past the halfway point."

"Those two end up together, but they split up first."

Then she went to cut fruit.

You rolled your eyes hard enough to hurt.

Episode fourteen: the one in the suit.

Episode twenty-three: the family line opened up, and no, she wasn't.

Episode thirty: they split. Episode thirty-six: they came back.

You sat there holding the remote, feeling read — not by the show, by your mother.

It took you a while to understand.

She isn't psychic. She's just seen too much.

Everything you dismiss as formula, she has been watching since she was young. Hundreds of times. It stopped being knowledge and turned into instinct.

The platform has a database. She has thirty years.

And she walked off right after. She never stays to gloat.

Because being right was never the point.

She just wanted to stand next to you for two minutes and say a few things.
en.editorNote: For the person whose parent can spoil an entire series in two minutes flat; also good for the moment they're proven right again and you'd rather not admit it
variations: Extended: her accuracy has a range. Romance, family lines, who is secretly related to whom — almost never wrong. Put on a detective story and she'll watch three minutes, say what even is this, and go do something else.

Reversal: one day it's your turn. She's watching something new, you pass through the living room, stand there for two minutes, and a guess falls out of your mouth. Three episodes later you're right, and the look she gives you is exactly the one you used to give her.

items.sourceNote: PChome 新聞關於追劇帶動取景地觀光與「同款照」熱潮的報導，原創改編為劇迷實地朝聖卻對不上畫面的情境

zh-tw.content:
你查到那場戲是在哪裡拍的，然後你真的去了。

地址存在手機裡，出站還走錯一次方向。

找到的時候你先愣住。

比想像中小很多。

那面牆就是一面普通的牆，旁邊機車停成一排，隔壁的店正在裝修，電鑽聲一直沒停過。

沒有配樂，沒有那場雨，也沒有人站在那裡等另一個人。

你還是把手機舉起來，試著把角度對上。

對不太起來。劇裡是仰角，還打了燈；你這張逆光，右下角卡著一台停在紅線上的機車。

你拍了幾張，其中一張你自己也知道不好看，但你留著。

旁邊有個人也在做一樣的事。你們沒有交談，只是互相讓了一下位置，然後各拍各的。

回程你才想通一件事。

你要來的不是這個地方。

這裡什麼都沒變，變的是你把那場戲看進去的那段日子。

你想站進那段日子裡一下下，而地址是唯一查得到的東西。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個為了一部劇特地跑去取景地、結果現場正在施工的朋友；也適合在被問「那裡到底有什麼好看」的時候直接當回答
variations: 延伸版：也有反過來的時候。你根本沒特地去，只是經過，抬頭覺得這個路口很眼熟。你站在原地把記憶翻出來對照，然後在毫無準備的情況下，被自己追過的劇偷襲一下。
反轉版：還有一種結局是撲空。你照著網路上的資訊找過去，那家店已經收了，鐵門拉下來，上面貼著搬遷公告。你在門口站了一會兒，覺得自己來晚了——晚到的不只是這家店。

en.content:
You looked up where that scene was filmed, and then you actually went.

The address sat in your phone, and you still left the station heading the wrong way.

When you found it, you stopped short.

Much smaller than you pictured.

The wall is just a wall. Scooters parked in a row beside it. The shop next door is being gutted, and the drill has not let up.

No score. No rain. Nobody standing there waiting for somebody else.

You raised your phone anyway and tried to match the angle.

It doesn't match. The show shot from below and lit it; yours is backlit, with a scooter on a red line wedged into the corner.

You took a few. One of them you know is bad, and you kept it.

Someone nearby was doing the same thing. Neither of you said anything. You stepped aside for each other and went back to your own frames.

On the trip back it finally landed.

The place was never what you came for.

Nothing here has changed. What changed is the stretch of your life when that scene got into you.

You wanted to stand inside that stretch for a moment, and an address is the only part of it you can look up.
en.editorNote: For the friend who traveled to a filming location and found scaffolding; also a ready answer when someone asks what there is to see there
variations: Extended: it happens in reverse too. You didn't plan anything, you were just passing, and an intersection looked familiar. You stood there matching it against a memory, ambushed by a show you finished long ago.

Reversal: sometimes you arrive too late. You follow the directions and the shop is gone, shutters down, a relocation notice taped to the metal. You stand outside for a bit, feeling like you missed something bigger than a shop.

items.sourceNote: 儂儂關於醫療職人陸韓劇寫實度的推薦專題，原創改編為「劇裡演的剛好是你那一行」的內行人對照清單

zh-tw.content:
劇裡演的剛好是你那一行，追劇就會變成另一種活動。

他們的辦公室有一整面落地窗，看出去是夜景。
你們那間的窗戶對著隔壁棟的外牆，還有一台冷氣主機。

他們接到棘手的案子，開一次會就有人拍桌說「這件我扛」。
你們光是決定誰去回那封信，就要來回三輪。

主角摔門走人，隔天回來位子還在，主管還問他吃飽沒。
你連請假都要先想好三個版本的說法。

他們的螢幕上永遠只開一個視窗，字很大，畫面很乾淨。
你的螢幕現在有十四個分頁，其中三個你不敢關。

最誇張的是，那件大事做完，就真的結束了。
沒有結案報告，沒有下一件，沒有人在群組裡問「那個什麼時候可以給我」。

你一邊看一邊哼了兩聲。

然後你每一集都看完了。

因為你要的從來不是準確。

你只是想看看，有人把你每天在做的那些事，拍得像一件重要的事。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個看到自己行業的劇就會邊看邊吐槽的朋友；也適合在同事問「你們那行真的長這樣嗎」的時候直接貼出來
variations: 延伸版：這種劇還有一個副作用，是親戚會拿它來問你。有人一臉認真地問你們是不是也常常那樣，你想解釋，講到第二句就發現對方要的其實不是答案，只是想聊那部劇。
反轉版：偶爾也會遇到拍得很準的。準到某一場戲你得按暫停，因為那個場面你上個月才真的經歷過。那時候你才知道，原來不準比較好看，準的會痛。

en.content:
When the show happens to be about your line of work, watching becomes a different activity.

Their office has a full wall of glass with a city view.
Yours faces the side of the next building and an air conditioning unit.

A hard case lands, they hold one meeting, and somebody hits the table and says they'll take it.
You need three rounds of email just to settle who answers the client.

The lead storms out, comes back the next day, desk intact, and the boss asks whether they've eaten.
You rehearse three versions of a sentence before asking for a day off.

Their monitors show exactly one window, enormous type, nothing else.
You have fourteen tabs open and three you're afraid to close.

Best of all, once the big thing is done, it's done.
No closing report. No next one. Nobody in the group chat asking when they can have that file.

You make a noise at the screen.

And then you watch every episode.

Because accuracy was never what you wanted.

You just want to see someone film the thing you do all day as though it mattered.
en.editorNote: For the friend who heckles every show set in their own industry; also a reply when a coworker asks whether your job is really like that
variations: Extended: these shows have a side effect — relatives use them as source material. Someone asks you in complete seriousness whether it's really like that, and two sentences in you can tell they don't want an answer, they want to talk about the show.
Reversal: occasionally one gets it right. So right that you hit pause mid-scene, because you lived that exact room last month. That's when you learn inaccurate is easier to watch. Accurate hurts.

items.sourceNote: 2026 下半年陸劇新劇片單整理，原創改編為熟悉演員在新劇與別人配對時的觀眾心情

zh-tw.content:
新劇第一集，鏡頭一帶，那張臉出現。

你心裡冒出一句完全不理性的話：

「他怎麼在這裡？」

更糟的是，他旁邊站著另一個人，光看走位你就知道等一下會發生什麼。

你的理智很清楚：那是工作，是另一個角色，另一個名字，另一套衣服。

你的情緒不接受。

你甚至替上一部裡那個女生覺得有點委屈——一個不存在的人。

你點開留言區，果然全部都是同一種語氣：

「先說好，我還沒原諒他。」

「等一下，你們兩個不是那種關係。」

然後你看到第三集就好了。

新的這一對也很好，你甚至覺得他們更配。

這才是最尷尬的地方。

你以為自己很專一。

其實你只是很聽鏡頭的話。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個看到愛的演員在新劇跟別人配對就受不了的朋友；也適合在自己三集內就變心的時候拿來自首
variations: 延伸版：這件事有更難的版本，是兩部同時在播。你星期三看他跟這個人吵架，星期五看他跟那個人和好，兩邊的情緒都是真的，你的腦子只好自己想辦法分裝。
反轉版：也有反效果。有一對演完之後大家都很喜歡，於是他們又被湊在一起拍了一部。你滿心期待點開，看兩集就覺得不太對——原來當初讓你嗑到的不是他們，是那個劇本。

en.content:
New show, first episode, the camera moves, and there's that face.

Something completely unreasonable surfaces in your head:

"What is he doing here?"

Worse, there's another person standing next to him, and the blocking alone tells you where this is going.

Your rational side has it handled: it's a job, a different character, a different name, a different wardrobe.

Your feelings decline to cooperate.

You even feel a little bad for the woman in the last show. Who does not exist.

You open the comments, and everyone is using the same tone:

"For the record, I have not forgiven him."

"Excuse me, you two are not that to each other."

By episode three you're fine.

The new pair is good. You might even like them better.

Which is the embarrassing part.

You thought you were loyal.

You just do whatever the camera tells you.
en.editorNote: For the friend who can't handle their favorite actor being paired with somebody new; also a confession for when you switch allegiance within three episodes
variations: Extended: the hard version is two shows airing at once. Wednesday he's fighting with one person, Friday he's making up with another, both are real while you're watching, and your head has to keep them in separate containers on its own.

Reversal: it can backfire. A pair goes over so well that they get cast together again. You start the new one thrilled, and two episodes in something is off — what you loved was never the two of them. It was the script.

items.sourceNote: udn 女子漾 2026 年 6 月韓劇清單報導，原創改編為外語劇中突然出現熟悉語言與招牌時的觀眾反應

zh-tw.content:
追了很久的外語劇，某一集裡有個路人開口，講的是你的母語。

你整個人坐直。

那句話發音有點歪，聲調全跑掉，但你聽得懂。

下一顆鏡頭掃過背景，招牌上的字你也認得。

你退回去重看那一段。再退一次。

你不是在確認演技，你是在確認自己有沒有看錯。

然後你截圖丟進群組，只打一句：有看到嗎。

群組炸了。大家全部卡在同一格畫面，有人開始爭論那幾個字是不是繁體，有人說那塊招牌根本是道具組亂拼的。

奇怪的是，那一格對劇情一點都不重要。

那個角色講完就走掉，之後再也沒出現。

可是那天你記得的就是那一格。

你已經看了那麼多集別人的世界。

突然有人把你的世界，放進了那個世界的角落。

就算只是背景，就算只是一塊招牌。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個在外語劇裡聽到熟悉語言就立刻截圖的朋友；也適合貼在為了一塊招牌吵起來的追劇群組裡
variations: 延伸版：這種瞬間還有翻譯版。字幕把那句母語轉成另一種語言，你聽到的跟讀到的打架，一邊聽懂一邊被翻錯，那種微妙的優越感只有你自己知道。
反轉版：當然也有讓人尷尬的版本。那個角色設定是你的同鄉，一開口卻是完全不通的腔調，還配上一堆沒有人會做的動作。你笑出來，然後有點想關掉。

en.content:
You've been with this foreign show a long time, and then an extra opens their mouth and speaks your language.

You sit straight up.

The pronunciation is bent, every tone is wrong, and you understand it perfectly.

The next shot pans across the background, and you can read the sign.

You scrub back and watch it again. Then again.

You're not checking the acting. You're checking whether you imagined it.

So you screenshot it into the group chat with one line: did you see this.

The chat detonates. Everyone is stuck on the same frame, arguing about the characters on the sign, someone insisting the art department assembled it out of spare parts.

The strange thing is that the frame doesn't matter at all.

That character says the line, walks off, and never comes back.

And it's the part of the day you remember.

You've spent all these episodes inside somebody else's world.

And for a moment, someone put your world in the corner of it.

Even as background. Even as a sign.
en.editorNote: For the friend who screenshots the instant a familiar language turns up in a foreign series; also fits a group chat that spent an evening arguing about one storefront sign
variations: Extended: there's a subtitled version of this moment. The subs render that line into another language, so what you hear and what you read disagree, and you get a small private superiority nobody else in the room can access.

Reversal: sometimes it lands badly. The character is supposedly from where you're from, opens their mouth in an accent from nowhere, and comes with gestures no one has ever made. You laugh, and then you want to turn it off.

items.sourceNote: 影劇通 2026 年 7 月暑假強檔片單整理，原創改編為開學前趕進度的集數換算

zh-tw.content: 離開學剩兩個禮拜。這部劇剩四十集。這不是排程問題，是體能問題。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個暑假最後兩週還在拚片單的人
variations: 進階版：你算過了，一天三集剛好趕上。你沒算的是你還要睡覺。
反轉版：後來你沒看完，開學那天你反而鬆一口氣，因為它還在。

en.content: Two weeks until school starts. Forty episodes to go. This isn't a scheduling problem, it's a stamina problem.
en.editorNote: For anyone speed-running a watchlist in the last stretch of summer break
variations: Extended: you did the math — three a day gets you there. You did not factor in sleeping.
Reversal: you never finished it, and on the first day back you were relieved, because it was still waiting.

items.sourceNote: 誠品 2026 追劇片單專題，原創改編為劇中季節與現實季節對不上的體感落差

zh-tw.content: 劇裡已經下了三場雪。你這邊還在開冷氣。同一張沙發，兩種天氣。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個八月在追冬天劇的朋友
variations: 延伸版：看到角色呼出白煙，你下意識拉了一下薄被，然後想起自己在流汗。
反轉版：等你追完，外面真的變涼了。你分不清是季節到了，還是你被劇騙進了秋天。

en.content: Three snowfalls in the show. The AC is still running on your end. Same couch, two climates.
en.editorNote: For the friend watching a winter series in August
variations: Extended: a character breathes out fog and you tug the blanket up, then remember you're sweating.
Reversal: by the time you finish, it really is cooler outside, and you can't tell whether the season arrived or the show talked you into fall.

items.sourceNote: Trip.com 2026 七夕（8/19）約會與活動整理，原創改編為當天在家開新劇的單人版過節方式

zh-tw.content: 七夕晚上，別人訂餐廳，我訂了一整季。位子只有一個，不用等。
zh-tw.editorNote: 七夕當天發限動用；也適合回覆問你有沒有約的人
variations: 延伸版：真的有人約的時候，你才發現最難的不是找人，是找一部兩個人都還沒看過的。
反轉版：朋友傳合照來炫耀，你回一句「我這邊也很甜」，然後螢幕裡那對正在分手。

en.content: Everyone's booking a restaurant tonight. I booked a whole season. Party of one, no wait.
en.editorNote: Post it on Qixi night; also a reply when someone asks if you have plans
variations: Extended: when someone does ask you out, the hard part isn't finding the person, it's finding a show neither of you has seen.
Reversal: a friend sends a photo to brag, you reply that things are sweet on your end too, and onscreen the couple is breaking up.

items.sourceNote: NOWnews 國人串流付費與收視習慣調查報導，原創改編為邊煮飯邊追劇的廚房日常

zh-tw.content:
你家廚房現在有一個固定位置，是給手機的。

它靠在醬油瓶上，角度剛好。

煮久了你發現，那餐好不好吃跟食譜沒關係，跟劇情有關係。

平靜的一集，蛋煎得漂亮。

螢幕裡有人開始吵架的那一集，鍋底就焦了。

你把焦掉的部分刮掉，繼續看。

反正這集也快演完了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個煮飯一定要配劇的室友
variations: 延伸版：你已經會用集數估時間了。這鍋大概要一集，那道菜半集。
反轉版：也有相反的時候。太好看的那幾集你乾脆不煮，直接叫外送，然後怪劇。

en.content:
There's a fixed spot in your kitchen now, and it belongs to your phone.

It leans against the soy sauce bottle at exactly the right angle.

After a while you notice the food doesn't depend on the recipe. It depends on the plot.

A quiet episode, and the eggs come out great.

The episode where somebody onscreen starts yelling, the pan scorches.

You scrape off the burnt part and keep watching.

It's almost over anyway.
en.editorNote: For the roommate who can't cook without an episode running
variations: Extended: you measure cooking in episodes now. This pot takes about one, that side dish takes half.
Reversal: sometimes the good episodes win, so you skip cooking, order delivery, and blame the show.

items.sourceNote: 簡單生活 Easylife 關閉 Netflix 自動播放下一集教學，原創改編為倒數跑完後把責任推給平台的心理

zh-tw.content: 「它自己播的。」倒數五秒你全程醒著，只是需要一個能怪的人。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個每次都說是平台害的朋友
variations: 延伸版：真的把它關掉之後，你才發現沒有人可以怪了。
反轉版：隔天你跟同事說是平台害的，同事說她昨天也被害了。

en.content: "It played itself." You were awake for all five seconds. You just needed someone else to blame.
en.editorNote: For the friend who blames the platform every single time
variations: Extended: once you actually turn it off, you find out there's nobody left to blame.
Reversal: you tell a coworker the platform did it to you, and she says it did the same thing to her.

items.sourceNote: FUNTOP 資訊網 Netflix 播放不中斷設定教學，原創改編為中場離席回來時倒數早已跑完的場景

zh-tw.content: 你起身去裝水，只是想證明自己停得下來。回來時下一集已經演到第三分鐘。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個每次中場離開都輸給倒數的人
variations: 延伸版：你回來還是坐下了，因為錯過的那三分鐘總得補回來。
反轉版：有一次你真的沒回去，隔天發現自己一點都不想知道後來怎樣。

en.content: You got up for water just to prove you could stop. You came back three minutes into the next episode.
en.editorNote: For anyone whose mid-show break never beats the countdown
variations: Extended: you sat back down anyway, because those three missed minutes had to be made up.
Reversal: one night you didn't go back, and by morning you didn't care how it ended.

items.sourceNote: 跳板俱樂部關閉 Netflix 預告與自動播放教學，原創改編為關掉功能後仍然自己手動連按下一集

zh-tw.content: 你把自動播放關掉了。那一晚你用手指按了四次下一集。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個以為問題出在功能上的朋友
variations: 延伸版：每一集都要自己按之後，你才知道那五秒其實是替你擋著羞恥。
反轉版：後來你又把它打開了，理由是這樣比較不用一直伸手。

en.content: You finally killed autoplay. That night your own finger hit next episode four times.
en.editorNote: For the friend who thought the feature was the problem
variations: Extended: once every episode needs a tap, you learn those five seconds were absorbing the shame for you.
Reversal: you switched it back on, and called it saving your arm the trouble.

items.sourceNote: 傑昇通信 Netflix「你還在看嗎」通知設定報導，原創改編為明知是謊還是要說出口的睡前宣告

zh-tw.content: 「再一集就好」講出來的當下，你就知道是假的。你還是講了。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個每晚都對自己說同一句話的人
variations: 延伸版：那句話不是承諾，是一個讓你安心繼續的儀式。
反轉版：有天你改口說要看到天亮，結果十一點就睡著了。

en.content: The second "just one more" leaves your mouth, you know it's false. You say it anyway.
en.editorNote: For the person who tells themselves the same line every night
variations: Extended: it isn't a promise, it's the small ritual that lets you keep going.
Reversal: one night you announced you'd stay up till dawn, and fell asleep at eleven.

items.sourceNote: 中嘉寬頻 2026 台劇推薦排行榜整理，原創改編為長期追劇在螢幕上留下的實體痕跡

zh-tw.content:
平板的螢幕上有一塊擦不掉的霧。

它不在角落，就在正中間偏下——那裡剛好是暫停鍵。

你用衣角擦過，用眼鏡布擦過，擦完亮兩天，它又慢慢浮回來。

那塊霧是這樣長出來的：有人按電鈴、鍋子滾了、群組有人問你在幹嘛、你想確認剛剛那句台詞是不是你聽到的意思。

一次一個指印，兩年下來變成一塊。

家裡最常被碰到的地方不是門把，是那裡。

買它的那天，你說是要拿來看書的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個平板螢幕永遠擦不乾淨的室友；也適合在被念「你多久沒擦螢幕」的時候回一句
variations: 延伸版：手機也有一塊，位置更下面一點，那是你單手拿著、拇指剛好搆得到的地方。
反轉版：有一次你認真擦乾淨了，結果開劇的第一分鐘你就又按了一次暫停。

en.content:
There's a smudge on the tablet screen that won't come off.

Not in a corner. Dead center, slightly low. Right where the pause button sits.

You've wiped it with your sleeve, with a lens cloth. It looks clean for two days, then it slowly comes back.

Here's how a smudge like that grows: someone rings the doorbell, the pot boils over, the group chat wants to know what you're up to, or you need to check whether that line meant what you think it meant.

One fingerprint at a time. Two years later, it's a patch.

The most-touched spot in your home isn't the doorknob. It's there.

The day you bought it, you said it was for reading.
en.editorNote: For the roommate whose tablet screen is never actually clean
variations: Extended: your phone has one too, a little lower, right where your thumb lands when you hold it one-handed.
Reversal: you finally cleaned it properly once, then hit pause in the first minute of the episode.

items.sourceNote: Marie Claire 2026「一追上癮」韓劇推薦片單，原創改編為深夜把睡眠時數換算成集數的算式

zh-tw.content:
鬧鐘設六點四十，現在一點二十。一集四十二分鐘。

你按計算機的手很穩：塞得下四集，還多九分鐘。

你算的不是還能睡多久，是還放得下幾集。這台計算機只認一種單位。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個半夜還在做數學的追劇同好
variations: 進階版：你撐到第二集就睡著，剩下的兩集額度隔天自動作廢。
反轉版：有一晚你真的看滿四集。鬧鐘響的時候你發現，時間算對了，人算錯了。

en.content:
Alarm set for 6:40. It is now 1:20. An episode runs 42 minutes.

Your hand is very steady on the calculator: four episodes fit, with nine minutes to spare.

You weren't working out how long you could sleep. You were working out how many episodes would fit. That calculator only knows one unit.
en.editorNote: For the friend still doing math at one in the morning
variations: Extended: you fell asleep during episode two, and the other two expired unused.
Reversal: one night you actually made it through all four. When the alarm went off, the math had been right and you had been wrong.

items.sourceNote: Yahoo 新聞 2026 上半年十大陸劇討論度排行報導，原創改編為前三集被當成入場費、日後卻最常回去看的落差

zh-tw.content:
朋友推坑的時候補了一句：「前三集有點悶，撐過去就好。」

你信了，也撐了。第四集開始果然好看，你一路看到完結。

半年後你想重看。

你點開的是第一集。

那三集裡沒有反轉、沒有誰要跟誰在一起，只有一群人吃早餐、坐公車、講一些不重要的話。

當初被你當成入場費的東西，現在是你唯一會回去的地方。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個當初叫你撐過前三集的人；也適合貼在有人問「這部要從第幾集開始看」的時候
variations: 延伸版：你後來也這樣推薦給別人，而且照樣叫他們撐過去。
反轉版：有一部你沒撐過去，第二集就放掉了。三年後你在別人的截圖裡看到那個畫面，才知道自己那時候關掉了什麼。

en.content:
When your friend talked you into it, they added a warning: "The first three episodes drag, just push through."

You believed them, and you pushed. Episode four picked up, and you rode it to the finale.

Six months later you wanted to rewatch it.

You opened episode one.

Nothing turns in those three episodes. Nobody gets together. It's a group of people eating breakfast, riding the bus, saying things that don't matter.

The part you treated as an entry fee is the only part you go back to now.
en.editorNote: For the friend who told you to push through the slow start
variations: Extended: you now recommend it the same way, warning the next person to push through.
Reversal: one show you didn't push through, you dropped in episode two. Three years later a screenshot showed you what you had switched off.

items.sourceNote: udn 售票網 2026 追劇片單專題，原創改編為週更等待與現實中等人回覆的耐心落差

zh-tw.content:
一部週更的劇要你等七天，你等得很有風度。

因為你知道是星期五晚上八點。知道了，星期三就好過了。

換成一個人，三小時沒回訊息，你把對話框點開了八次。

要是他也肯公告一個更新時間就好了。

你不是沒有耐心，你只是想知道那個東西什麼時候會來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個等劇很有耐心、等人完全沒有的朋友
variations: 延伸版：劇還有下週，人沒有。你撐得住那七天，是因為它保證會來。
反轉版：後來對方回了，只有一句「剛在忙」。你等的那三小時，比那句話長很多。

en.content:
A weekly show makes you wait seven days and you handle it with grace.

Because you know it lands Friday at eight. Knowing that is what gets you through Wednesday.

A person goes three hours without replying and you've opened the chat eight times.

If only people posted a release schedule.

It isn't that you have no patience. You just want to know when the thing is coming.
en.editorNote: For the friend who waits calmly for a show and not at all for a person
variations: Extended: the show has a next week, the person doesn't. You survive those seven days because they're guaranteed to end.
Reversal: they finally replied with two words about being busy. The three hours were much longer than the message.

items.sourceNote: Dcard 戲劇綜藝板深夜追劇串，原創改編為手機剩電與劇情剩秒數的雙倒數

zh-tw.content:
這集剩十一分鐘，手機剩百分之四。

充電線在房間，你在客廳，那六步路是今晚你走不出去的距離。

你把亮度壓到最暗，臉貼上去，像在跟一顆電池討價還價。

螢幕黑掉的那一秒，他剛好把話講到一半。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個追劇追到手機自動關機、還怪電池不爭氣的朋友
variations: 延伸版：你插上線等它復活，那三十秒你什麼都沒做，只是盯著那顆充電圖示。
反轉版：開機之後你發現進度沒存到，得從十一分鐘前重看——那句話你聽了兩次。

en.content:
Eleven minutes left in the episode. Four percent left on the phone.

The cable is in the bedroom, you're on the couch, and those six steps are the longest distance of your night.

You drop the brightness to nothing and hold the screen up to your face, haggling with a battery.

It goes black exactly halfway through his sentence.
en.editorNote: For the friend whose phone dies mid-episode and who blames the battery every time
variations: Extended: you plug it in and just stare at the charging icon for thirty seconds, doing nothing else.
Reversal: it boots back up and the progress didn't save, so you rewatch those eleven minutes and hear the line twice.

items.sourceNote: 2026 年 8 月熱門戲劇話題榜，原創改編為深夜超商偶遇同進度觀眾

zh-tw.content:
十一點半，你去超商買隔天的早餐。

結帳的時候你瞄到櫃檯後面那台小平板，畫面停在一個你昨天才看過的鏡頭。

你們同時抬頭，他說「你也……」，你說「第幾集」。

那晚你多買了一瓶飲料，他找錢找得特別慢，因為兩個人的進度還沒對齊。
zh-tw.editorNote: 深夜在超商、髮廊或計程車上撞見同一部劇的人之後，適合發一則限時動態
variations: 延伸版：你們沒有交換名字，只交換了一句「後面會更好看」，然後你走進夜裡笑了一路。
反轉版：他多講了一句話，你伸手把他嘴巴堵住——差一集，就是雷。

en.content:
Eleven thirty, you stop at the convenience store for tomorrow's breakfast.

At the register you catch the little tablet behind the counter, paused on a shot you watched yesterday.

You both look up at the same time. He starts with "You're also—" and you answer "What episode."

You buy an extra drink and he counts your change very slowly, because the two of you aren't synced yet.
en.editorNote: Post this after running into a stranger watching your show at a store, a salon, or in a cab
variations: Extended: you never traded names, only "it gets better," and you grinned the whole walk home.
Reversal: he said one sentence too many and you put a hand up to stop him. One episode ahead is a spoiler.

items.sourceNote: Dcard 追劇板家中固定座位討論，原創改編為沙發擬人開口說話

zh-tw.content:
如果你家的沙發會講話，它會先報一組數字。

右邊那一格凹下去的深度，是左邊的三倍。

它會說你這兩個月沒換過位置，說你有四次是在那裡醒來的，說有一晚你抱著抱枕，肩膀抖了很久。

它知道的比誰都多，然後每天晚上安安靜靜地，讓你再坐下去一次。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合配一張自家沙發凹痕的照片發文，或傳給總說「我很少看電視」的自己
variations: 延伸版：抱枕也想補一句——它被抓過幾次，它都記得是哪幾集。
反轉版：那天你換坐左邊，看不到十分鐘就站起來了，原來位置也是劇的一部分。

en.content:
If your couch could talk, it would open with a number.

The right cushion has sunk three times deeper than the left one.

It would say you haven't switched seats in two months, that you woke up there four times, that one night you held a pillow and your shoulders shook for a while.

It knows more than anyone, and every night it quietly lets you sit back down.
en.editorNote: Pair with a photo of the dent in your own couch, or send to yourself the next time you claim you barely watch TV
variations: Extended: the pillow wants to add something. It remembers exactly which episodes it got squeezed during.
Reversal: you tried the left side once and stood up within ten minutes. Turns out the seat is part of the show.

items.sourceNote: 2026 串流平台方案與片庫規則報導，原創改編為下架倒數逼出拖延已久的片單

zh-tw.content:
你點開清單裡那部劇，封面右上角多了一行小字：剩 14 天。

你囤了它八個月，理由每次都一樣——等有空、等心情對、等一個完整的週末。

那天晚上你連看六集，中間一次都沒有起身。

治好你拖延症的不是週末，是那行倒數。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給片單囤了一整年、永遠說「等有空再看」的那個人
variations: 延伸版：剩兩天的時候，你把最後四集排進行事曆，標題寫「重要會議」。
反轉版：期限過了它又續約回來，你反而再也沒點開過。

en.content:
You open your list and there's new small print on the cover: 14 days left.

You've been saving that show for eight months, always for the same reasons — free time, the right mood, one clean weekend.

That night you watched six episodes without standing up once.

What cured your procrastination wasn't the free weekend. It was the countdown.
en.editorNote: For the person with a year-old watchlist who keeps saying they'll get to it eventually
variations: Extended: with two days left you blocked the final four episodes into your calendar under "important meeting."
Reversal: the license got renewed and it stayed. You never opened it again.

items.sourceNote: OTT 話題劇集討論熱度榜，原創改編為觀眾自己先查角色生死的自我爆雷行為

zh-tw.content:
第十九集結束，你沒有按下一集，你打開了搜尋框。

你輸入那個角色的名字，後面加了三個字：還在嗎。

你很清楚這一查，懸念就沒了，但你更撐不住接下來四十分鐘的心臟。

查完你鬆了一口氣，然後對著一部已經沒有懸念的第二十集，看到凌晨兩點。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個嘴上最恨爆雷、自己卻先偷查結局的朋友
variations: 延伸版：你查到的答案是「後面有解釋」，你盯著那五個字，比原本更慌。
反轉版：有一次你忍住沒查，那集播完你在沙發上坐了十分鐘沒動——你才知道自己躲掉的是什麼。

en.content:
Episode nineteen ends and instead of hitting next, you open a search bar.

You type the character's name and add two words: still alive.

You know the suspense dies the moment you read the answer, but you can't survive another forty minutes of that heartbeat.

You exhale, then watch a now completely spoiled episode twenty until two in the morning.
en.editorNote: For the friend who hates spoilers loudest and still looks up the ending first
variations: Extended: the answer you found was "it gets explained later," and those four words made you more anxious, not less.
Reversal: one time you didn't look. The episode ended and you sat on the couch for ten minutes, finally understanding what you'd been dodging.

items.sourceNote: 2026 Netflix 方案與同戶裝置、同時觀看上限說明，原創改編為家人之間互讓觀看名額的瞬間

zh-tw.content:
表姊的訊息跳出來的時候，畫面正好轉圈：裝置數量已滿。

你打了「我第八集，你先看」，手指在送出鍵上停了三秒。

她回一句「不用啦我明天再補」，後面加了個笑臉。

你按下繼續播放，這一集的前五分鐘完全沒進到你腦子裡。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個永遠先讓你看完再說的家人。
variations: 延伸版：你後來自己辦了一個方案，開通的第一件事是把她加成額外成員。
反轉版：隔天你才知道那句明天再補是騙你的，她凌晨兩點已經看到第十二集。

en.content:
Your cousin's message lands right as the screen starts spinning: device limit reached.

You type back "I'm on episode eight, go ahead," and hover over send for three seconds.

She replies "nah, I'll catch up tomorrow," with a smiley face tacked on.

You hit resume, and the first five minutes of the episode never make it into your head.
en.editorNote: For the family member who always tells you to go ahead first.
variations: Extended: you eventually got your own plan, and the first thing you did was add her as an extra member.
Reversal: "tomorrow" was a lie, and she was already on episode twelve by two in the morning.

items.sourceNote: 短劇與短影音節奏分析報導，原創改編為用幾分鐘解說代替正片、被人當場問倒

zh-tw.content:
午休聊到那部話題劇，你接得很順。

誰背叛了誰、誰在雨裡跪了整夜、最後那通電話有多狠，你講得比誰都激動。

直到有人問你，女主角在醫院走廊坐著的那三分鐘你怎麼看，你腦中一片空白。

你「追完」的那個版本，全長八分鐘，標題寫著一次看完。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個用解說影片把三十集塞進一個午休的朋友。
variations: 延伸版：那天晚上你默默打開正片，走廊那三分鐘你看了兩次，什麼都沒發生，你卻停在那裡。
反轉版：後來你發現問你的人也沒看正片，他記得那三分鐘，是因為另一支解說拿它當封面。

en.content:
At lunch the table gets onto the show everyone is talking about, and you keep right up.

Who betrayed who, who knelt in the rain all night, how cold that last phone call was, you tell it louder than anyone.

Then someone asks what you made of the three minutes where she just sits in the hospital hallway, and your head goes empty.

The version you "finished" ran eight minutes, under a title promising the whole story in one sitting.
en.editorNote: For the friend who fits thirty episodes into one lunch break with recap videos.
variations: Extended: that night you quietly opened the real thing, watched those hallway minutes twice, and nothing happened in them at all.
Reversal: the person who asked hadn't watched it either, and only knew that scene because another recap used it as the thumbnail.

items.sourceNote: 2026 六大串流平台使用心得比較，原創改編為首頁演算法推薦列把觀眾口味整排攤開

zh-tw.content:
首頁那一排寫著「因為你看了那部」，底下擺了三個推薦。

第一個是同一個男演員的另一部戲，你上禮拜才嫌它的海報醜。

第二個是你三年前看到第二集就放生的老劇，它記得比你清楚。

第三個是你從來沒跟任何人承認過會看的類型，位置還放在正中間。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個被首頁推薦列看穿的朋友。
variations: 延伸版：你按了「不感興趣」，隔天它換一張封面，回到同一格。
反轉版：你點開第三個，看到凌晨一點，最後還回頭給它按了大拇指。

en.content:
The row on the home screen says "because you watched that one," with three picks lined up under it.

The first is another show with the same lead actor, the one whose poster you mocked last week.

The second is a series you abandoned at episode two three years ago, and it remembers that better than you do.

The third is a genre you have never admitted to anyone that you watch, sitting right there in the middle.
en.editorNote: For the friend the recommendation row has completely figured out.
variations: Extended: you tapped "not interested," and the next day it came back to the same slot with a new cover image.
Reversal: you opened the third one, watched until one in the morning, and then went back and gave it a thumbs up.

items.sourceNote: 串流平台聲量與話題劇討論榜，原創改編為陪人重看自己愛劇時忍住不爆雷的心情

zh-tw.content:
先別出聲。

他才按下第一集，而你已經知道第七集會對人做什麼。

先把嘴閉好，先把手機收起來，先裝成你也是第一次看。

等他看到那個地方，你再轉頭看他的臉，那才是你今晚真正要看的。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個坐在旁邊等你看到某一集表情的人。
variations: 延伸版：他按了暫停，轉頭問你那個人是不是要走了，你只回三個字：繼續看。
反轉版：那次你沒忍住，第三集就把結局講出來，他之後都改成自己一個人看。

en.content:
Say nothing yet.

He just started episode one, and you already know what episode seven does to people.

Keep your mouth shut, put your phone away, and act like this is your first time too.

When he reaches that part, turn and look at his face, because that is the thing you actually came to watch tonight.
en.editorNote: For the person sitting next to you, waiting for your face at a certain episode.
variations: Extended: he paused and asked whether that character was about to leave, and you said only two words: keep watching.
Reversal: one time you couldn't hold it in, spoiled the ending by episode three, and he has watched alone ever since.

items.sourceNote: 第二螢幕與邊做事邊看劇的觀看行為研究，原創改編為做家事時被一句台詞打中的場景

zh-tw.content:
陽台的衣架被風推著轉了半圈，你一件一件夾上去，耳機裡那部劇還在往下播。

夾到第五件的時候，那個角色講了一句很短的話，你手裡還捏著袖子，整個人沒動。

衣服被風吹得啪一聲，你才想起來自己在太陽底下站了多久。

回房間你把那一段重播，這次你先把門關好，讓自己哭出來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個在做家事的時候被一句台詞打中、還要假裝是被太陽曬到的人。
variations: 延伸版：你回頭把那一集從頭看，發現那句話前面還有兩句更狠的，你當下完全沒聽見。
反轉版：隔天你把同一段放給室友聽，他說還好啊，你才知道那句話只對你有用。

en.content:
The drying rack spins half a turn in the wind while you clip up shirts one at a time, the show still running in your earbuds.

On the fifth shirt a character says something short, and you just stand there with a sleeve still bunched in your hand.

A gust snaps the laundry loud enough to remind you how long you've been out in full sun.

Back inside you replay that part, close the door first, and finally let yourself cry.
en.editorNote: For the friend who got wrecked by one line mid-chore and blamed it on the heat.
variations: Extended: you rewatched the whole episode and found two harder lines right before it that you never even heard the first time.
Reversal: you played the clip for your roommate, they shrugged, and that's how you learned the line was only ever aimed at you.

items.sourceNote: 追劇統計中的中途棄劇與反覆重開行為，原創改編為半年卡在同一集的量化敘事

zh-tw.content:
這半年你把同一部劇打開了十一次，每次都停在第四集。

第一次是真的想睡了，第二次是有人按門鈴，剩下那九次連藉口都懶得找，手指自己就滑掉了。

進度條記得比你清楚，每次回來都停在同一格，像在等你給個交代。

你沒有給，你點了第十二次，然後又停在同一個地方。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個片單裡有一部劇卡了半年、每個禮拜都說要看完的人。
variations: 延伸版：第十三次你乾脆先跳到大結局，看完再回頭補中間，順序亂七八糟但你終於看完了。
反轉版：朋友問你那部好不好看，你講得頭頭是道，內容有八成是你在網路上看來的。

en.content:
You've opened the same show eleven times in six months, and every time you stall out at episode four.

First time you were sleepy, second time someone rang the doorbell, and the other nine times you didn't even bother inventing a reason, your thumb just swiped away on its own.

The progress bar remembers better than you do, parking at the same spot every time like it's waiting for an explanation.

You never gave one, you opened it a twelfth time, and you died in the exact same place.
en.editorNote: For the friend with one show stuck in their queue since spring who still swears they'll finish it.
variations: Extended: on attempt thirteen you skipped straight to the finale, then filled in the middle backwards, and somehow that finally worked.
Reversal: a friend asked if the show was any good and you had a whole take ready, most of it borrowed from strangers online.

items.sourceNote: 2026 年 8 月古裝陸劇話題榜與網友討論，原創改編為把生活異狀與劇情進度連成因果的自嘲

zh-tw.content:
自從那部宮廷劇演到第三十集，我家的洗衣機就開始發出怪聲。

我沒有拿去修，我把追劇的時間從半夜改成早上。

怪聲停了，那個被關進冷宮的人也活著走出來了。

這兩件事我不打算分開講。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個把生活裡所有巧合都算在劇情頭上的人。
variations: 延伸版：後來洗衣機真的壞了，那天剛好播大結局，我一點都不意外。
反轉版：室友請師傅來看，說是排水管卡住，我聽完點點頭，心裡還是相信自己那一套。

en.content:
Ever since that palace drama hit episode thirty, my washing machine started making a noise.

I never called a repair guy. I moved my watching from midnight to morning.

The noise stopped, and the character they'd locked away in the cold palace walked back out alive.

I'm not going to pretend those are two separate stories.
en.editorNote: For the friend who credits every coincidence in their life to whatever they're currently watching.
variations: Extended: the machine finally died on finale night, and honestly, that tracked.
Reversal: my roommate got a technician in who blamed the drain hose, I nodded politely and kept my own theory.

items.sourceNote: 串流觀看環境與習慣調查，原創改編為多工追劇卻關不掉電視的清單

zh-tw.content:
追劇的時候我的手不會閒著，會剪指甲，會剝橘子，會把明天要吃的藥先分好。

耳朵也很忙，聽得出來誰在說謊，聽得出來配樂什麼時候要轉。

連暫停的時機都被我練得很準，走去冰箱拿罐飲料，回來一格都沒漏掉。

只有一件事我到現在還做不好，片尾曲跑完之後把電視關掉。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個一心多用超強、偏偏永遠關不掉電視的人。
variations: 延伸版：後來我學會在片尾曲的時候先起身，走到門口再回頭看一眼，然後又坐回去了。
反轉版：那天我真的關掉了，客廳一安靜下來，我馬上開了另一部。

en.content:
My hands never idle while a show is on. I clip my nails, I peel an orange, I sort out tomorrow's pills.

My ears are working too, catching who's lying and hearing exactly when the score is about to turn.

I've got the pause timing down cold, fridge run for a drink, back before a single frame slips by.

There's one thing I still can't manage, and that's turning the TV off once the end credits finish rolling.
en.editorNote: For the multitasker who can do anything during a show except end it.
variations: Extended: now I stand up during the credits, walk to the door, look back once, and sit right back down.
Reversal: one night I actually turned it off, the living room went quiet, and I had something else playing within a minute.

items.sourceNote: 重看／沉浸式觀看的情緒調節研究，原創改編為健身房更衣室的旁觀場景

zh-tw.content: 更衣室最裡面那格，有個人已經換好一半，一隻鞋帶綁好了，另一隻就這樣垂在地上。她把手機立在置物櫃門邊，眼睛沒離開過，肩膀跟著什麼東西縮了一下又鬆開。門開了又關，冷風灌進來，她連頭都沒抬，只是把身體再往櫃子那邊靠近了兩公分。我沒立場笑她，因為我的上衣已經拿在手上四分鐘，我這集也還剩三分鐘。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個說要去運動、結果在更衣室卡住半小時的健身夥伴。
variations: 延伸版：後來我們在飲水機前碰到，兩個人都沒講話，因為兩邊的片尾曲還沒放完。
反轉版：她比我早走，我還站在原地，才發現整間更衣室只剩我一個人沒換好衣服。

en.content: There's someone at the far end of the locker room who's only half changed, one shoe laced and the other still hanging open. She's propped her phone against the locker door and her eyes haven't left it, her shoulders tightening and easing at something I can't see. The door swings, cold air comes through, and she doesn't look up once, she just leans two inches closer to the screen. I'm in no position to laugh at her, because I've been holding my shirt for four minutes and I've still got three left in this episode.
en.editorNote: For the gym buddy who said they were going to work out and stalled in the locker room.
variations: Extended: we ran into each other at the water fountain later and neither of us said a word, because both sets of end credits were still rolling.
Reversal: she left before I did, and I looked around to find I was the only person in the room still not dressed.

items.sourceNote: 連續觀看與習慣化／事後懊悔的研究，原創改編為洗車機裡的自問場景

zh-tw.content: 車子開進洗車機，水一潑上來，我為什麼第一個動作是解鎖手機？五分鐘到底能看什麼，一段預告，還是上一集最後那三分鐘？泡沫把前擋整片蓋住的時候，我盯著轉圈圈的載入符號，是在等訊號還是在等別的？洗完出來，玻璃亮得刺眼，而我對這場洗車唯一的記憶，是刷子壓過車頂那陣悶悶的聲音，剛好蓋掉了那句我最想聽清楚的台詞。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合配一張洗車機泡沫糊住車窗的照片發限動。
variations: 延伸版：我把那段倒回去重聽了三次，第三次才確定他說的是「我等你」還是「我等過你」。
反轉版：那天我什麼都沒點開，看著泡沫從擋風玻璃上滑下來，居然覺得比任何一集都好看。

en.content: The car rolls into the wash, the water hits the glass, and why is unlocking my phone the very first thing I do? What can five minutes actually hold, a trailer, or the last three minutes of the previous episode? When the foam covers the whole windshield and I'm staring at a spinning loader, am I waiting on the signal or on something else entirely? I come out the other side with the glass blinding me, and the only thing I remember about the wash is the dull drag of the brushes across the roof, landing right on the one line I most wanted to hear.
en.editorNote: Pair it with a photo of foam smearing down the windshield.
variations: Extended: I scrubbed back three times and still couldn't tell whether he said "I'll wait" or "I waited."
Reversal: that day I didn't open anything, and watching the foam slide down the glass beat every episode I'd queued up.

items.sourceNote: 劇終失落感（post-series depression）報導，原創改編為候診區追劇警語條列

zh-tw.content:
追劇專用．候診區使用須知
一、進場前請先確認耳機兩邊都有聲音，本區不受理因單邊播放造成的劇情誤解。
二、本集若含哭戲，請自備面紙，護理站那盒是給打針的人用的。
三、聽見自己的名字被叫到時，請立即暫停，不得以「剩一分半」為由拖延。
四、暫停的位置請自行記牢，本裝置不保證下次回診時你還記得看到哪。
五、離開診間後三十公尺內禁止續播，以免走到馬路上還在替別人擔心。
六、若出現「醫生剛剛講什麼我一句都沒聽進去」之情形，請重新掛號。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個每次看病都要提早半小時到、只為了多看兩集的人。
variations: 延伸版：第七條，等候時間超過四十分鐘者，本區默許你把一整季看完。
反轉版：那天叫號叫得特別快，我反而有點希望前面還有五個人。

en.content:
Waiting Room Viewing Guidelines
1. Confirm both earbuds are working before you sit down. Plot confusion caused by one-sided audio is not our problem.
2. If this episode has a crying scene, bring your own tissues. The box at the nurses' station is for people getting shots.
3. Pause immediately when your name is called. "Ninety seconds left" is not an accepted reason to stall.
4. Memorize where you paused. Nothing guarantees you'll remember it by your next appointment.
5. No resuming within a hundred feet of the exit, or you'll cross the street still worrying about someone fictional.
6. If you can't recall a single word the doctor said, please book another appointment.
en.editorNote: For the friend who shows up thirty minutes early just to get two more episodes in.
variations: Extended: rule seven, if the wait exceeds forty minutes, you are hereby cleared to finish the whole season.
Reversal: the queue moved fast that day and I caught myself wishing five more people were ahead of me.

items.sourceNote: 重看熟悉影集作為壓力調節的報導，原創改編為圖書館自習室桌面盤點

zh-tw.content:
自習室靠窗第三張桌子，今天的清點結果：
原文書一本，攤在第 74 頁，昨天也是第 74 頁。
螢光筆三支，只有黃色那支動過，畫的是課本上「本章重點」那四個字。
保溫瓶一個，水位從早上到現在只降了兩公分。
平板一台，立在筆袋後面，角度剛好只有我看得到。
字幕開著，音量調到零，光看嘴型也猜得出他在說什麼。
借書證一張，壓在桌角，今天唯一被翻開的是它右邊那份播放清單。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個佔位佔了一整天、進度卻停在同一頁的讀書會同伴。
variations: 延伸版：第八項，計時器一個，設定二十五分鐘，今天已經被我按掉十一次。
反轉版：隔壁那位收書的時候我瞄了一眼，他的螢幕也是暗的，我們大概是同一種人。

en.content:
Third desk by the window in the study room, today's inventory:
One textbook, open to page 74, same page as yesterday.
Three highlighters, only the yellow one used, on the words "key concepts" already printed in the margin.
One thermos, water level down two centimeters since morning.
One tablet, standing behind the pencil case at an angle only I can see.
Subtitles on, volume at zero, close enough to read his mouth anyway.
One library card, pinned under the corner, and the only thing opened today is the playlist next to it.
en.editorNote: For the study-group friend who held the seat all day and never turned the page.
variations: Extended: item eight, one timer set to twenty-five minutes, dismissed eleven times so far today.
Reversal: I glanced over as the guy beside me packed up, and his screen was dark too, so we're probably the same kind of person.

items.sourceNote: 自動播放移除停止線索的研究報導，原創改編為加油站自助加油機報修工單

zh-tw.content:
報修單編號 A-2261｜自助加油區三號機
故障描述：加油結束後畫面卡在「請取收據」，車主在原地站了六分鐘
到場檢查：機器一切正常，油槍已歸位，車主耳機只掛著一邊
處理方式：站員輕拍肩膀，車主抬頭回一句「等他把那句話講完」
客戶確認：收據已取，車已駛離
結案備註：本站不負責劇情，只負責油
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個連加油都要先按暫停的朋友，配一張油槍歸位的照片剛好。
variations: 延伸版：追加一件，同日二號機也是同一位車主，這次卡在「請選擇油品」。
反轉版：那位站員後來自己也跟著追了，隔週的報修單多出一行「站員亦已入坑」。

en.content:
Service Ticket A-2261 | Self-serve pump #3
Reported fault: screen stuck on "Take your receipt," driver standing there six minutes
On-site check: pump normal, nozzle holstered, one earbud hanging off his shoulder
Action taken: attendant tapped his shoulder, driver looked up and said "let him finish the sentence"
Customer confirmation: receipt taken, car gone
Closing note: we handle the fuel, not the plot
en.editorNote: For the friend who has to hit pause before they can pump gas.
variations: Extended: second call, same day, pump #2, same driver, this time frozen on "select fuel grade."
Reversal: the attendant started the show himself, and next week's log picked up a line reading "attendant now also hooked."

items.sourceNote: 串流介面設計誘導連續觀看的研究，原創改編為家用網路報修案件紀錄

zh-tw.content:
案件編號 N-0819｜家用網路報修
客戶申告：入夜以後畫質自己掉到最模糊那一階，臉都糊了
現場實測：線路正常，速率達標，路由器沒問題
初判原因：同一戶四台裝置，同時在看同一部劇的不同集數
建議處置：請住戶自行協調觀看順序，本公司不受理爆雷衍生之糾紛
客戶回覆：那我先讓我媽看，她進度最前面
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個跟家人搶頻寬、還得互相封口的追劇同盟。
variations: 延伸版：補充備註，隔週同址再報一次，這回是四個人搶著看同一集。
反轉版：工程師收工前小聲問了一句：「所以那部到底叫什麼名字？」

en.content:
Case N-0819 | Home internet repair
Customer report: after dark the picture drops to the blurriest setting, faces turn to mush
Field test: line clean, speeds at spec, router fine
Preliminary cause: four devices in one household streaming four different episodes of the same show
Recommended action: household agrees on a viewing order; spoiler disputes fall outside our scope
Customer reply: fine, my mom goes first, she's furthest ahead
en.editorNote: For the household alliance that fights over bandwidth and then swears each other to silence.
variations: Extended: follow-up, same address the next week, all four now fighting over the same episode.
Reversal: the tech stopped at the door and asked, quietly, what the show was called.

items.sourceNote: 追劇時數與觀看習慣統計，原創改編為追劇小桌二手刊登文

zh-tw.content:
售 追劇專用摺疊小桌 一張
使用狀況：買來兩年，展開的次數遠比收起來的次數多
附贈：手機立架一支、擦不掉的杯漬三圈
瑕疵欄：右下角一道裂痕，某部劇大結局那晚被我手肘撞的
售出原因：換了張更大的，這張撐不住我新的追劇姿勢
面交地點：學校側門，七點以後我都在，別問我劇情
zh-tw.editorNote: 二手社團刊登文的口吻，配一張桌面杯漬特寫最有味道。
variations: 延伸版：補充說明，桌面那三圈杯漬會依角度反光，官方說法叫使用痕跡。
反轉版：貼了三天沒人問，我把它搬回房間，然後又把它展開了。

en.content:
For sale: one folding lap desk, binge-grade
Condition: two years old, unfolded far more often than folded away
Included: one phone stand, three cup rings that will not come off
Flaws: crack in the bottom right corner, elbowed it the night a finale aired
Reason for selling: got a bigger one, this can't hold my new watching posture
Pickup: side gate of the school, after seven, don't ask me about the plot
en.editorNote: Written like a resale-group listing; pair it with a close-up of the cup rings.
variations: Extended: note, the three rings catch the light from certain angles. The official term is patina.
Reversal: three days, no messages. I carried it back to my room and unfolded it again.

items.sourceNote: 2026 熱門韓劇片單報導，原創改編為早餐店爆雷對話

zh-tw.content:
「昨天那集你追了沒？」
「看到一半，蛋餅端上來就分心了。」
「所以你還不知道他最後把那枚戒指丟去哪囉？」
「先別講，拜託你先別講。」
「我沒講啊，我只是說有個東西被丟掉了而已。」
「你已經講了。我這杯冰奶茶現在喝起來一點味道都沒有。」
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個每次都堅稱自己沒爆雷的早餐同伴。
variations: 延伸版：「那我幫你把吸管插好，當作補償。」「太晚了，戒指已經在我腦裡飛了。」
反轉版：我回家補完才發現，戒指根本沒被丟掉，他只是講得很像。

en.content:
"Did you get to last night's episode?"
"Halfway. Then my breakfast showed up."
"So you don't know where he ends up throwing the ring?"
"Don't. I'm begging you, don't."
"I didn't say anything. I just said something got thrown."
"You said it. My iced milk tea tastes like nothing now."
en.editorNote: For the breakfast buddy who insists, every single time, that they didn't spoil anything.
variations: Extended: "Let me at least put your straw in." "Too late, that ring is already airborne in my head."
Reversal: I got home, finished it, and the ring never goes anywhere. He just made it sound like it did.

items.sourceNote: 2026 小說改編影視片單整理，原創改編為二手書店書架前的慢動作特寫

zh-tw.content:
她的指尖沿著書背滑過去，停在那本書口翻到發黑的原著上。
手收回來一次，又伸出去，這次多花了三秒才把它從架上抽下來。
她翻到中間某一頁，眼睛沒有動，肩膀先垮了一格。
二手書店的老闆在櫃檯後面按著計算機，沒有抬頭，也沒有問她為什麼站在原地那麼久。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個追完劇就跑去找原著的人，配一張書架側光照最有味道。
variations: 延伸版：她把書放回架上，走到門口又折回來，這次直接走到櫃檯。
反轉版：抽下來才發現，書裡夾著上一位讀者的手寫紙條，寫著「第七章別在深夜看」。

en.content:
Her fingertips slide along the spines and stop on the one with the darkened page edges, the novel the show came from.
Her hand pulls back once, goes out again, and takes three extra seconds to work the book free of the shelf.
She opens to a page somewhere in the middle, her eyes don't move, and her shoulders drop first.
Behind the counter the used-bookstore owner taps at his calculator, never looking up, never asking why she has been standing there so long.
en.editorNote: For the friend who finishes a show and goes straight out to hunt down the book; pair it with a side-lit shot of the shelf.
variations: Extended: she puts it back, gets as far as the door, turns around, and this time walks straight to the counter.
Reversal: once it was off the shelf she found a previous reader's note inside, saying don't read chapter seven late at night.

items.sourceNote: 長時間連續觀看的心理影響研究，原創改編為圖書館自習室隔板的獨白

zh-tw.content:
我是自習室第十四桌的隔板，我這一面看到的東西比書多。
左邊那位攤開的課本停在同一頁四十分鐘，桌面的光倒是換過九種顏色。
她把耳機線繞在食指上，一集播完就鬆開，下一集開始又繞回去。
閉館廣播響起時她合上了書，螢幕還亮著，正在載入下一集。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個帶著課本去自習、結果進度全推在別的地方的人。
variations: 延伸版：我這一面還記得她三月的樣子，那時候在桌面換顏色的是螢光筆。
反轉版：隔天她坐下來，先把手機翻成面朝下，撐了整整二十六分鐘。

en.content:
I'm the divider on desk fourteen in the library study room, and my side sees more screens than pages.
The textbook on my left has stayed open to the same page for forty minutes, while the light on the desk has changed color nine times.
She winds the earbud cord around her finger, lets it unspool when an episode ends, winds it back when the next one starts.
The closing announcement plays and she shuts the book, and the screen is still lit, loading the next one.
en.editorNote: For the person who packs a textbook for a study session and makes progress on something else entirely.
variations: Extended: my side still remembers her in March, when the thing changing colors on this desk was a highlighter.
Reversal: the next day she sat down, turned her phone face down first, and held out for a solid twenty-six minutes.

items.sourceNote: 連續追劇與睡眠、情緒關聯的系統性回顧，原創改編為操場跑道上的倒敘時間軸

zh-tw.content:
天亮的時候我在學校操場跑道上走完第七圈，鞋子是濕的，腦子是空的。
往回推兩小時，我在床上按下了那個我發誓再也不按的鍵。
再往回推，是同事午休時丟了一句「最後三集完全變了一個樣」。
而最早的最早，只是我前一天路過走廊，聽見有人講到一個角色的名字，順手搜了一下。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個熬夜追完、隔天用走路贖罪的人。
variations: 延伸版：走到第八圈我開始盤算剩下的兩集，然後決定今晚大概也不用睡了。
反轉版：走到第十圈才想起來，同事講的其實是另外一部。

en.content:
By sunrise I had walked seven laps of the school track, shoes wet, head empty.
Two hours before that, I was in bed pressing the button I had sworn I would never press again.
Further back, a coworker mentioned over lunch that the last three episodes turn into a completely different show.
And the very beginning: I walked past a hallway the day before, heard someone say a character's name, and looked it up.
en.editorNote: For the friend who binges all night and does penance the next morning on foot.
variations: Extended: on lap eight I started doing the math on the two episodes left, and decided tonight was probably a write-off too.
Reversal: it took until lap ten to remember my coworker had been talking about a different show entirely.

items.sourceNote: 週末長時間串流與眼睛疲勞的報導，原創改編為眼鏡行驗光室的現場實況

zh-tw.content:
驗光師正把那台機器推到我面前，要我看清楚裡面那條路的盡頭。
我正在努力對焦，浮出來的卻是昨晚那個長鏡頭收尾的畫面。
他問我最近是不是常在暗暗的房間裡盯螢幕，我正在計算要誠實到第幾成。
他把鏡片轉了一格，字忽然變清楚，而我在想這個清晰度剛好夠我看完下一集的字幕。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個坐進驗光室才回想起自己上一季追了幾部的人。
variations: 延伸版：他把試戴鏡框遞過來，我第一件事是拿起手機確認字幕會不會變好看。
反轉版：走出驗光室我才發現，招牌上的字我本來就看得見，我只是很久沒抬頭了。

en.content:
The optometrist is rolling the machine up to my face, asking me to look at the far end of the road inside it.
I'm trying to focus, and what surfaces instead is the closing frame of a long take I watched last night.
He's asking whether I've been staring at screens in dim rooms lately, and I'm calculating exactly how honest to be.
He clicks the lens wheel one notch, the letters snap clean, and I'm thinking this is sharp enough to get me through the subtitles of the next episode.
en.editorNote: For the friend who only tallies up last season's shows once they're sitting in the exam chair.
variations: Extended: he hands me a trial frame and the first thing I do is pick up my phone to see whether subtitles look better in it.
Reversal: outside the shop I realized I could always read the sign across the street. I just hadn't looked up in a while.

items.sourceNote: 康健雜誌談追劇的情緒投射與代入感，原創改編為動物醫院診療台的現場

zh-tw.content:
獸醫把聽診器收起來，說一切都好，而我站在那張診療台旁邊哭了出來。
牠今天早上叫聲有點啞，我抓了提籠一路衝過來，事情本來只有這麼多。
真正壓垮我的是昨天半夜——某部劇的第二十二集，一隻橘貓沒能撐到主角推開門。
那滴眼淚昨天就備好了，只是拖到今天，借了一隻健康的貓當作落下來的地方。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個看完動物題材的劇之後，隔天就把家裡的毛小孩抓去做全身檢查的人。
variations: 延伸版：獸醫問我最近牠有沒有哪裡怪怪的，我差點回答『牠沒有，有問題的人是我』。
反轉版：回程牠在提籠裡睡得很沉，我把那一集重看了一遍，這次先翻到結局才敢按下播放。

en.content:
The vet puts the stethoscope away, says everything looks fine, and I start crying next to the exam table.
My cat's meow sounded hoarse this morning, I grabbed the carrier and rushed over, and that's genuinely all that happened.
What actually broke me was last night — episode twenty-two of a show where an orange cat doesn't make it to the door opening.
That tear was ready yesterday. It just held on until today and borrowed a perfectly healthy cat as a place to land.
en.editorNote: For the friend who watches one show with an animal in it and books a full checkup for their pet the next morning.
variations: Extended: the vet asked if anything about her seemed off lately, and I nearly said "she's fine, I'm the one with the problem."
Reversal: she slept through the whole ride home while I rewatched that episode, this time reading the ending first before I dared press play.

items.sourceNote: 天下雜誌報導追劇可滿足社交需求，原創改編為夜市套圈圈攤前的獨白

zh-tw.content:
你搬走以後我還是會晃到那個套圈圈的攤子前面，站著看別人丟。
你以前老說這攤穩賺不賠，圈的直徑永遠比獎品底座小那麼一點點，講完還是照丟不誤。
我們看到第九集就擱下的那部劇，上個月完結了，我自己補完了。
倒數第二集有個橋段，你一定會笑到必須暫停。我照樣暫停了，然後整個房間只有我在笑。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個曾經和你共用一組帳號、後來各自散在不同城市的人。
variations: 延伸版：老闆問我要不要試一次，我說我朋友比較會丟，話出口才想到他已經三年沒回過這條街。
反轉版：我最後還是丟中了一隻醜醜的娃娃，抱回家擺在沙發你以前坐的那一側，正對著螢幕。

en.content:
You moved away, and I still drift over to that ring-toss stall and stand there watching other people throw.
You always said the game was rigged, that the rings were a hair narrower than the prize bases, and then you'd throw anyway.
That show we abandoned at episode nine finished airing last month. I got through the rest of it alone.
There's a bit in the second-to-last episode you would have had to pause for. I paused too, and then the whole room was just me laughing.
en.editorNote: For the person you used to share a streaming login with, before you both ended up in different cities.
variations: Extended: the stall owner asked if I wanted a turn, and I said my friend is the one who's good at this, then remembered he hasn't been down this street in three years.
Reversal: I actually landed one in the end, an ugly little plush, and set it on the side of the couch that used to be yours, facing the screen.

items.sourceNote: MIC 台灣影音觀看行為調查（訂閱平台數與月花費），原創改編為田邊產業道路上的今昔對照

zh-tw.content:
高中放學那幾年，我騎車經過這條田邊的產業道路，只想快點回家守八點檔。
沒有暫停，沒有回放，漏掉一句台詞就是真的漏掉了，隔天上課要靠同學口述補回來。
同一條路，同一個彎，我現在會把車停下來，手機裡躺著四個平台、七部沒看完的劇。
想倒回三十秒隨時都可以，可是我已經很久沒有為了誰把油門催到底。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個手上訂閱越開越多、片單卻越積越厚的老同學。
variations: 延伸版：以前錯過的那部八點檔，現在整季都在平台上，我囤了兩年，一集也沒點開。
反轉版：那天我在彎道邊把車熄火，什麼也沒看，就聽了十分鐘的蛙叫，那是我這個月最長的一段不快轉。

en.content:
Back in my high school years I'd ride this farm road home, and the only thing on my mind was making the eight o'clock drama.
No pausing, no rewinding — miss a line and it was gone, and the next day at school a classmate had to recite it back to me.
Same road, same bend, except now I pull over. My phone holds four platforms and seven shows I never finished.
I can jump back thirty seconds whenever I want, and I haven't floored it to get home for anyone in a very long time.
en.editorNote: For the old classmate whose subscription list keeps growing while the watchlist grows faster.
variations: Extended: the drama I kept missing back then is sitting there in full, all seasons, and I've had it saved for two years without opening a single episode.
Reversal: that night I cut the engine at the bend and watched nothing at all, just ten minutes of frogs, the longest stretch I've gone this month without skipping ahead.

items.sourceNote: 報導提及先查結局的觀眾共感力較高，原創改編為配鎖店裡被一句閒話翻轉意義的片段

zh-tw.content:
配鎖的師傅把胚料壓上砂輪，火花濺開的那幾秒，我低頭把一段預告看完了。
他沒有抬頭，只問我要配幾把，我說兩把好了，剩下那把先收著。
旁邊推門進來的阿姨接了半句閒話：「收起來的那一把，多半是留給不會再過來的人。」
師傅笑了一聲，我沒笑。我原本只是嫌那部劇的女主角鑰匙配得太多把，走出店門才知道我心疼的其實不是劇裡的人。
zh-tw.editorNote: 傳給那個看劇看到某個道具就會突然安靜下來的人。
variations: 延伸版：我把新配好的那把塞進外套內袋，一路捏著它走回家，像捏著一個還沒播出的結局。
反轉版：隔週我又去了一次，這次只配一把。師傅什麼也沒問，阿姨也不在，這件事就真的只是配一把鑰匙。

en.content:
The locksmith presses the blank against the wheel, and in the few seconds of sparks I finish watching a trailer.
He doesn't look up, just asks how many I want. Two, I say, and I'll hold on to the spare.
A woman coming through the door tosses out half a thought: "the one you hold on to is usually for someone who isn't coming back."
He laughs. I don't. I'd only been annoyed that the lead in that show gets copies made in every other episode, and it wasn't until I was outside that I understood who I'd actually been aching for.
en.editorNote: For the friend who goes quiet mid-episode because of one small prop.
variations: Extended: I tucked the new key into my coat pocket and squeezed it the whole walk home, like an ending that hasn't aired yet.
Reversal: I went back the next week and ordered just one. He asked nothing, the woman wasn't there, and it was finally only a key.

items.sourceNote: 報導串流平台要求共享帳號各檔案綁定獨立信箱，原創改編為共用片單被時間拉開距離的片段

zh-tw.content:
雲端資料夾裡那個叫「晚上一起看」的片單，上一回被誰動過，還留在去年十一月。
上禮拜三我為了翻報稅資料又點進去，縮圖仍舊是那張海報，右上角卻換成「已退出共用」。
同一個資料夾，兩個時間點，片單裡一部片也沒少，少掉的是那個會把新片丟進來的人。
我把它拖進封存，然後很沒出息地又拖了回來。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給剛結束一段關係、卻還沒動手清雲端的朋友。
variations: 延伸版：後來我在那份片單裡多加了三部，加的時候還是會下意識想「他應該會嫌太長」。
反轉版：某天縮圖旁邊又亮起小綠點，代表有人正在瀏覽。我什麼都沒做，只是把手機翻過來繼續讓它亮著。

en.content:
The shared folder still has a playlist called "watch together tonight," last touched in November of last year.
Wednesday I opened it while hunting for tax paperwork; same cover art, except the corner now reads "left the share."
Same folder, two timestamps, not a single title missing — what's missing is the person who used to drop new ones in.
I dragged it to archive, then pathetically dragged it right back out.
en.editorNote: For a friend who's out of the relationship but hasn't cleared out the shared drive.
variations: Extended: I've added three more since, and every time I still catch myself thinking he'd say it's too long.
Reversal: One night a little green dot appeared beside it — someone was browsing. I did nothing, just turned my phone face down and let it glow.

items.sourceNote: 報導串流平台新制影響共用帳號用戶，原創改編為三人共享進度表在續訂前後的落差

zh-tw.content:
共用的雲端資料夾裡有一份追劇進度表，續訂之前我打開對過一次，那時三個人各自卡在不同集數。
繳完這期費用的隔天再開，欄位被拉成整整齊齊的一條線，因為另外兩個人都改成了「棄追」。
中間只隔二十六小時，我卻花了一整晚，才有力氣把自己那格從七集往後推一集。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合在群組裡只剩你還在追、其他人早就跑光的時候發。
variations: 延伸版：我沒有刪掉他們兩格，留著比較像有人陪，雖然那兩格永遠不會再動。
反轉版：半年後其中一個人偷偷把自己那格改回來，還往前補了十集。我裝作沒看見，隔天默默追到跟他一樣。

en.content:
Our shared folder holds a viewing tracker. Before the renewal went through I opened it once, and the three of us were stuck on different episodes.
The day after the payment cleared I opened it again: the column had straightened into one tidy line, because the other two had both switched to "dropped."
Twenty-six hours apart, and it still took me a whole night to find the energy to move my own cell up by one episode.
en.editorNote: Post this when you're the last one in the group chat still watching.
variations: Extended: I didn't delete their rows. Keeping them feels like company, even though they'll never move again.
Reversal: Half a year later one of them quietly changed his row back and jumped ten episodes ahead. I pretended not to notice, then caught up to him overnight.

items.sourceNote: 文章解析自動播放與陪伴感如何讓人停不下來，原創改編為同一組沙發在兩個時期的擺法

zh-tw.content:
去年剛裝好投影機那晚，我們把沙發往後推了半公尺，說這樣才像戲院。
昨天我又把同一張沙發推回牆邊，一個人看的時候，多出來的半公尺只讓房間更空。
機器沒壞，劇也還在更新，變的只是推沙發的手從兩雙剩下一雙。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合搬完家或分開住之後，重新一個人開機看劇的那個晚上。
variations: 延伸版：我後來把亮度調高兩格，因為原本那個設定是配合他怕刺眼的眼睛。
反轉版：上個月朋友來借住三天，沙發又被推出去半公尺。他走的那天我沒推回去，就先這樣放著。

en.content:
The night we finally set up the projector last year, we shoved the couch back half a metre and said now it feels like a cinema.
Yesterday I pushed that same couch back against the wall, because watching alone, the extra half metre only makes the room emptier.
Nothing broke, the show is still airing; the only change is that pushing the couch went from four hands to two.
en.editorNote: For the first night you power everything on alone after moving out.
variations: Extended: I turned the brightness up two notches, since the old setting was calibrated for his eyes, not mine.
Reversal: A friend crashed here for three nights last month and the couch went out half a metre again. The day he left I didn't push it back.

items.sourceNote: 報導指出主動查劇透者情感投射較強，原創改編為兩則相隔一個多月的訊息對照

zh-tw.content:
上個月十九號的深夜，她在聊天室說：「這部我幫你留著，等你有空我們一起看。」
這禮拜二一樣的鐘點，一樣的聊天室，她說：「我看完了，你自己慢慢追沒事。」
中間我連著加班十七天，播放器很貼心地把進度停在片頭曲。
兩句話擺在一起像同一句話的正面跟背面，被日子翻了個面。
我沒有回訊息，只是把那部劇拉到清單最底下，換我讓它等一下。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合放在那種「我沒空追劇」其實是「我沒空經營關係」的深夜。
variations: 延伸版：後來我補完了，還特地挑她說最好哭的那集重看，好像這樣就能跟她同場。
反轉版：我終於騰出一個週末，開口約她重看一次。她回：「好啊，不過我要邊看邊爆雷。」

en.content:
Late on the nineteenth of last month she messaged: "I'm saving this one for you, we'll watch it when you're free."
Tuesday this week, same hour, same chat: "I finished it. Take your time, it's fine."
In between I worked seventeen days straight, and the player thoughtfully parked me on the opening credits.
Set side by side, the two lines are the front and back of one sentence, flipped over by the days between them.
I didn't reply. I just dragged the show to the bottom of my list, so this time it could wait for me.
en.editorNote: For the late night when "no time to watch" really means "no time for us."
variations: Extended: I did finish it eventually, and rewatched the episode she called the saddest, as if that counted as watching together.
Reversal: I finally cleared a weekend and asked her to rewatch it with me. She said sure — but she'd be spoiling it the whole way through.

items.sourceNote: 調查指出逾七成觀眾的收看高峰落在晚間六到十點、單次多看兩三集，原創改編為同一天三個不同地點的短鏡頭

zh-tw.content:
末班車第三節車廂，有人靠著門睡著，手機還亮著上一集的片尾曲。
早餐店的電視轉到重播的鄉土劇，老闆娘一邊煎蛋一邊跟著唸台詞。
影印機吐紙吐得很慢，我趁那十幾秒看完了一場告白。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合貼在那種一整天都在偷看幾分鐘劇、卻沒有一次看完整的日子。
variations: 短版：車上有人睡著，早餐店在重播，影印機前我看完一場告白。
延伸版：那天回到家我反而沒開電視，好像今天的份已經零零散散地看夠了。

en.content:
Third car of the last train out: someone asleep against the door, phone still lit with the end credits of the previous episode.
The breakfast shop TV has switched to a rerun of an old family serial, and the owner mouths the lines while she flips an egg.
The copier feeds paper painfully slowly, and I got through an entire confession scene in those fifteen seconds.
en.editorNote: For the kind of day you steal a few minutes of a show everywhere you go and never finish one episode.
variations: Short: Someone asleep on the train, a rerun at the breakfast shop, a confession scene at the copier.
Extended: I didn't switch anything on when I got home. Somehow the day's quota had already been used up in pieces.

items.sourceNote: 報導提到近七成國人付費訂閱影音平台、追劇已成日常，原創改編為三個互不相干的夜間場面

zh-tw.content:
麵攤老闆把小電視轉向自己那一側，湯滾了也沒回頭。
末班車上有人開外放看完最後五分鐘，整節車廂被迫一起聽到大結局。
我家的燈沒開，播放器問我還在不在，問了兩遍。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合深夜下班後、發現全世界都在陪自己看劇的那種時刻。
variations: 短版：老闆沒回頭，車廂被迫聽完結局，我家的播放器問了兩遍。
延伸版：後來我把外放那個人追的劇也加進清單，理由是他撐到最後一分鐘都沒關掉。

en.content:
The noodle stall owner has angled the little TV toward himself; the broth boils over and he doesn't turn around.
Someone on the last train plays the final five minutes on speaker, and the whole car is dragged through the finale with him.
My lights are off at home, and the player asks twice whether I'm still there.
en.editorNote: For the late walk home when it seems the entire city is watching something with you.
variations: Short: The owner never turns around, the train car hears the finale, my player asks twice.
Extended: I added the speaker guy's show to my own list afterward, purely because he stayed to the last minute without turning it off.

items.sourceNote: 報導串流平台推出整季離線下載、讓觀眾隨時隨地都能接著看，原創改編為三個地點各自播放的畫面

zh-tw.content:
剪髮店的鏡子裡，設計師的手機立在吹風機旁邊，正在演一場葬禮。
跑步機上那個人邊跑邊笑，耳機線垂下來跟著晃。
我把進度條往回拖了十秒，因為剛剛在回一則訊息。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合用在「明明整天都在看，卻什麼劇情都沒記住」的自首時刻。
variations: 短版：鏡子裡在辦葬禮，跑步機上有人在笑，我把十秒重看一次。
延伸版：那十秒我又拖回去兩遍，第三遍才發現漏掉的是一個沒有台詞的鏡頭。

en.content:
In the salon mirror, the stylist's phone is propped beside the blow dryer, playing a funeral.
On the treadmill a man runs and laughs at once, his earbud cord swinging along.
I dragged the progress bar back ten seconds, because I was answering a message.
en.editorNote: For confessing that you watched all day and remember none of the plot.
variations: Short: A funeral in the mirror, laughter on the treadmill, ten seconds rewound at my desk.
Extended: I pulled those ten seconds back twice more, and only on the third pass noticed the thing I'd missed was a shot with no dialogue in it.

items.sourceNote: 文章談台劇後勁強到讓人熬夜追完，原創改編為三個地方各自沉在同一齣劇裡的畫面

zh-tw.content:
圖書館四樓的耳機孔壞了一半，插上去只剩左邊有配樂。
球場旁的長椅上，兩個穿制服的把同一支手機橫著擺，一人分一邊耳機。
末班車進站的風把瀏海吹起來，畫面裡剛好有人跑向月台。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合放在一齣劇跟著你走過一整天、連回家的路上都還沒放過你的時候。
variations: 短版：左耳有配樂，長椅上分一邊耳機，進站的風跟畫面同時來。
延伸版：後來我特地重看那個月台鏡頭，發現配樂其實是從右邊進來的，那一整天我都少聽了一半。

en.content:
The headphone jack on the library's fourth floor is half dead, so only the left channel carries the score.
On the bench by the courts, two kids in school uniforms prop one phone sideways and split a pair of earbuds.
The wind off the arriving last train lifts my fringe, and on screen someone happens to be running for a platform.
en.editorNote: For when one show follows you through an entire day and still won't let go on the way home.
variations: Short: Score in the left ear only, one earbud each on the bench, the wind and the platform arriving together.
Extended: I rewatched that platform shot later and found the score actually enters from the right, which I never heard once.

items.sourceNote: 報導談重看舊作與懷舊對情緒的作用，原創改編為兩個時間點的耳機狀態對照

zh-tw.content:
高三那年，掃具間最裡層的鐵架上塞著一副白色耳機，午休四十分鐘剛好夠看半集。
那副耳機的海綿掉了一邊，我照樣塞著，聽得見的那半邊就是全部。
耳機還在，午休沒了，一集四十五分鐘要切成三個晚上才看得完。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合傳給那個把追劇時間從午休一路搬到深夜的同學。
variations: 短版：耳機還在，午休不見了，半集變成三個晚上。
延伸版：那副耳機我沒丟，插進新手機才知道孔已經不合了。

en.content:
Senior year, a white pair of earbuds sat on the back rack of the broom closet, and forty minutes of lunch was exactly half an episode.
The foam pad on one side was long gone, and I wore them anyway, because the half I could hear was the whole thing.
The earbuds are still here, the lunch break isn't, and a forty-five-minute episode takes three nights to finish.
en.editorNote: For the classmate whose watching hours migrated from lunch break all the way into the middle of the night.
variations: Short: The earbuds survived, the lunch break didn't, and half an episode turned into three nights.
Extended: I never threw those earbuds out, and only found out the jack no longer fits when I plugged them into a new phone.

items.sourceNote: 文章談重複回看熟悉影集的普及化，原創改編為同一個拖把桶前後兩個時間點的群體追劇

zh-tw.content:
國一的掃具間門後空著一格，我們把手機立在拖把桶上，四個人擠著看週更劇。
拖把桶換過一次，藍的換成灰的，劇也演到第三季。
灰的那個桶還在原地，看劇的人各自回到各自的房間，群組裡只剩「你看了嗎」四個字。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合貼給當年一起擠著看、現在各自在不同時區追同一部的朋友。
variations: 短版：桶還在，人散了，群組裡只剩一句「你看了嗎」。
延伸版：後來我們四個誰也沒追完那一季，倒是每年都還會提起那個桶。

en.content:
In seventh grade the broom closet had one empty slot behind the door, so we propped a phone on a mop bucket and four of us crowded around a weekly release.
The bucket got replaced once, blue swapped for gray, and the show made it to season three.
The gray one is still in the same corner, the four of us went back to four separate rooms, and all that's left in the group chat is "did you watch it yet."
en.editorNote: For the friends you once crowded around one phone with, now watching the same show in different time zones.
variations: Short: The bucket stayed, the crowd didn't, and the group chat is down to one question.
Extended: None of the four of us ever finished that season, but we still bring up that bucket every year.

items.sourceNote: 台劇片單報導提到週播與整季上架的觀看差異，原創改編為客廳電視前後兩代的等待方式

zh-tw.content:
二十年前那台映像管電視要等九點整，廣告一進來，全家散開去做各自的事。
同一部劇整季躺在片單裡，隨時能按，四十集排成一列，等人點開。
廣告沒了，等九點的人也沒了，客廳的燈一年比一年開得晚。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合放在你發現「隨時可以看」之後反而更少看的那天。
variations: 短版：廣告沒了，等九點的人也沒了，四十集排成一列沒人動。
延伸版：我媽現在還是九點坐下來，只是手上拿的是遙控器加一支手機。

en.content:
Twenty years ago the tube TV in the living room meant waiting until nine sharp, and when the ads came on the whole family scattered to do their own things.
The same show now sits in the list as a full season, ready whenever, forty episodes lined up waiting for someone to press play.
The ads are gone, so is the nine o'clock wait, and the living room light goes on later every year.
en.editorNote: For the day you realize that being able to watch anytime somehow means watching less.
variations: Short: The ads are gone, the nine o'clock wait is gone, and forty episodes sit there untouched.
Extended: My mom still sits down at nine, except now she's holding a remote and a phone at the same time.

items.sourceNote: 談重看熟悉影集帶來安全感的專文，原創改編為制服口袋痕跡與現今集數的對照

zh-tw.content:
高中制服左邊口袋被手機撐出一塊方形的印子，那三年一部劇最多十三集。
制服洗到領口發黃，那塊印子沒有跟著淡掉。
今年這部演到第二十四集，我把手機架在桌上，兩隻手空出來，反而不知道要放哪裡。
zh-tw.editorNote: 適合放在你發現追劇姿勢換了、集數變多、人卻沒有比較輕鬆的時候。
variations: 短版：口袋的印子沒淡，集數卻從十三集變成二十四集。
延伸版：那件制服還掛著，我把手機架在它前面，播的是同一部劇的重製版。

en.content:
My high school uniform had a square mark on the left pocket where the phone stretched it out, and back then a show ran thirteen episodes at most.
The uniform faded to yellow at the collar, and that square mark never faded with it.
This year's show is on episode twenty-four, I prop the phone on the desk, both hands free, and now I have no idea where to put them.
en.editorNote: For when you notice the posture changed and the episode counts grew, and none of it made watching feel any lighter.
